newsitem.title: CANADA: HORSE RACING-HARNESS DRIVER HENRI FILION DIES AFTER TRACK MISHAP.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-HARNESS DRIVER HENRI FILION DIES AFTER TRACK MISHAP.

text.p: Henri Filion, a member of one of the most famous families in harness racing, died Wednesday, four days after an accident at the Hippodrome track. He was 56.
Filion was in the lead driving Bye Bye Angus in Saturday's ninth race when the horse went off stride and fell, throwing Filion to the track.

Filion walked off the track and refused medical treatment, track officials said. He later complained of chest pain, according to Callie Davies-Gooch, media relations coordinator for the Canadian Trotting Association.
Filion was taken to a hospital where he was diagnosed with six broken ribs and a punctured lung. He was moved to intensive care Sunday, but developed pneumonia and died Wednesday.

Henri, the younger brother of harness racing legend Herve Filion, won 3,318 races and earned more than $21 million during his career. His older brother has won more than 14,000 races in his Hall of Fame career. In total, the Filion family has won a total of 27,791 harness races.
Fellow driver Darrell Coville was dragged for 10 meters when his sulky locked wheels with Filion's rig in the accident.
"I didn't see everything because it happened so quickly. None of the drivers is talking about it much today," Colville said.
"It's hard to lose someone you know and work with, but like other drivers, I don't think about injuries. If you think about such things, you don't perform the way you should."
